I've been farming this land for over 40 years, since I was a boy helping my father. I only finished primary school, so I can't read those thick agricultural books, but I know my fields. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Lao Zhang down the road — when he tries something new and it works, I pay attention.

My wheat is already in the ground — I planted 10 mu last October with improved seed, did rotary tillage, and put down about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu. It's coming up green now. I'll irrigate four times this spring and summer, and spray for weeds and pests maybe four times. If the weather doesn't turn bad, I should get around 500 kg per mu.

After harvest in early June, I'll plant summer maize on that same 10 mu. No time to till — there's only about a week between wheat harvest and maize planting, so I'll use no-tillage and put in hybrid seed. Denghai 605 or something like it, whatever the seed shop has. I'll give it about 10 kg of nitrogen per mu and irrigate three times. Last year I got 550 kg per mu, and I expect about the same.

I also keep a small cotton plot — 3 mu. I plant it in late April with improved seed, rotary tillage. Cotton is a lot of work, maybe 16 sprays for bollworm and weeds, and I irrigate twice, but the autumn price is usually decent. I hope for 275 kg per mu. I thought about growing vegetables like some younger farmers, but my son works in Shijiazhuang and it's just me and my wife. Too much hand work. Wheat, maize, and a little cotton — that's what I know, that's what I can handle.
